question: Refer to the given calorimeter setup diagram. A copper calorimeter of mass $100\text{ g}$ ($s_{\text{Cu}} = 0.1\text{ cal/g }^\circ\text{C}$) contains $150\text{ g}$ of water at $20^\circ\text{C}$. A $50\text{ g}$ piece of metal at $100^\circ\text{C}$ is dropped into it. The final equilibrium temperature is $25^\circ\text{C}$. Find the specific heat capacity of the metal.
explanation: Heat Gained by (Water + Calorimeter) = $m_w s_w (25 - 20) + m_c s_c (25 - 20) = (150 \times 1 \times 5) + (100 \times 0.1 \times 5) = 750 + 50 = 800\text{ cal}$. Heat Lost by Metal = $m_m s_m (100 - 25) = 50 \times s_m \times 75 = 3750 s_m$. Equating: $3750 s_m = 800 \implies s_m = \frac{800}{3750} \approx 0.213\text{ cal/g }^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: Refer to the given heating curve. $10\text{ g}$ of ice at $-10^\circ\text{C}$ is mixed with $10\text{ g}$ of water at $50^\circ\text{C}$. What is the final equilibrium temperature of the mixture?
explanation: Heat lost by water cooling from $50^\circ\text{C}$ to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $Q_{\text{loss}} = 10 \times 1 \times 50 = 500\text{ cal}$. Heat needed to warm ice from $-10^\circ\text{C}$ to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $Q_1 = 10 \times 0.5 \times 10 = 50\text{ cal}$. Remaining heat available for melting ice: $500 - 50 = 450\text{ cal}$. Heat needed to melt ALL ice: $10 \times 80 = 800\text{ cal}$. Since $450 < 800$, only $\frac{450}{80} = 5.625\text{ g}$ of ice melts. Thus final equilibrium temperature is $0^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: $1\text{ g}$ of steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$ is passed into $1\text{ g}$ of ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$. What is the final equilibrium temperature of the mixture?
explanation: Heat required to melt $1\text{ g}$ ice and heat water to $100^\circ\text{C}$: $Q_{\text{req}} = (1 \times 80) + (1 \times 1 \times 100) = 180\text{ cal}$. Heat released by $1\text{ g}$ steam condensing at $100^\circ\text{C}$: $Q_{\text{release}} = 1 \times 540 = 540\text{ cal}$. Since $540 > 180$, only $\frac{180}{540} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ g}$ of steam condenses. Final temperature remains $100^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: A lead bullet of mass $m$ moving at speed $v = 300\text{ m/s}$ strikes a target and stops. If $50\%$ of its kinetic energy is converted into heat within the bullet, calculate the rise in temperature of the bullet. (Take $s_{\text{lead}} = 150\text{ J/kg K}$)
explanation: Heat absorbed $Q = 0.50 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} m v^2\right) = \frac{1}{4} m v^2$. Temperature rise $m s \Delta T = \frac{1}{4} m v^2 \implies \Delta T = \frac{v^2}{4 s} = \frac{300^2}{4 \times 150} = \frac{90000}{600} = 150^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: A block of ice of mass $50\text{ g}$ at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is dropped into $100\text{ g}$ of water at $30^\circ\text{C}$. Find the mass of ice remaining unmelted.
explanation: Heat released by water cooling to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $Q = 100 \times 1 \times 30 = 3000\text{ cal}$. Mass of ice melted $m_{\text{melted}} = \frac{Q}{L_f} = \frac{3000}{80} = 37.5\text{ g}$. Mass of ice remaining unmelted $= 50 - 37.5 = 12.5\text{ g}$.

subject: Physics
question: Three liquids A, B, and C of equal masses have temperatures $12^\circ\text{C}$, $19^\circ\text{C}$, and $28^\circ\text{C}$ respectively. When A and B are mixed, the temperature is $16^\circ\text{C}$. When B and C are mixed, the temperature is $23^\circ\text{C}$. Find the equilibrium temperature when A and C are mixed.
explanation: Mix A & B: $s_A(16 - 12) = s_B(19 - 16) \implies 4 s_A = 3 s_B \implies s_A = \frac{3}{4} s_B$. Mix B & C: $s_B(23 - 19) = s_C(28 - 23) \implies 4 s_B = 5 s_C \implies s_C = \frac{4}{5} s_B$. Mix A & C: $s_A(T - 12) = s_C(28 - T) \implies \frac{3}{4}(T - 12) = \frac{4}{5}(28 - T) \implies 15(T - 12) = 16(28 - T) \implies 15T - 180 = 448 - 16T \implies 31T = 628 \implies T \approx 20.25^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: An electric kettle has two heating coils. When one coil is used, water boils in $10\text{ minutes}$. When the other coil is used, water boils in $15\text{ minutes}$. If both coils are connected in parallel, the time required to boil the same quantity of water is:
explanation: Power in parallel $P_{\text{total}} = P_1 + P_2 \implies \frac{Q}{t} = \frac{Q}{t_1} + \frac{Q}{t_2} \implies \frac{1}{t} = \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{5}{30} = \frac{1}{6} \implies t = 6\text{ minutes}$.

subject: Physics
question: A refrigerator converts $100\text{ g}$ of water at $20^\circ\text{C}$ into ice at $-10^\circ\text{C}$ in $1\text{ hour}$. What is the average rate of heat extraction by the refrigerator in Watts? (Take $1\text{ cal} = 4.2\text{ J}$)
explanation: $Q_{\text{total}} = m s_w (20 - 0) + m L_f + m s_{\text{ice}} (0 - (-10)) = (100 \times 1 \times 20) + (100 \times 80) + (100 \times 0.5 \times 10) = 2000 + 8000 + 500 = 10500\text{ cal} = 10500 \times 4.2 = 44100\text{ J}$. Rate of heat extraction $P = \frac{Q}{t} = \frac{44100}{3600\text{ s}} = 12.25\text{ W}$.

question: Liquid water of mass $100\text{ g}$ at $100^\circ\text{C}$ is mixed with $10\text{ g}$ of steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$. The final state of the mixture is:
options: 110 g water at 100 degrees C with 10 g steam remaining
correctAnswer: 110 g water at 100 degrees C with 10 g steam remaining
explanation: Since both water and steam are already at $100^\circ\text{C}$, no net heat exchange takes place ($T_1 = T_2 = 100^\circ\text{C}$). The system remains a thermal equilibrium mixture of $100\text{ g}$ water and $10\text{ g}$ steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$.

question: A waterfall of height $h = 210\text{ m}$ discharges water. Assuming all gravitational potential energy lost is converted into internal thermal energy of water, the rise in temperature of water at the bottom of waterfall is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2, s_{\text{water}} = 4200\text{ J/kg K}$)
explanation: $m g h = m s \Delta T \implies \Delta T = \frac{g h}{s} = \frac{10 \times 210}{4200} = \frac{2100}{4200} = 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: $50\text{ g}$ of ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is mixed with $50\text{ g}$ of water at $80^\circ\text{C}$. The final temperature of the mixture will be:
explanation: Heat released by water cooling to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $Q = 50 \times 1 \times 80 = 4000\text{ cal}$. Heat needed to melt ALL $50\text{ g}$ ice: $50 \times 80 = 4000\text{ cal}$. Exactly $4000\text{ cal}$ is released, which melts all ice into water at $0^\circ\text{C}$. Final equilibrium temperature is $0^\circ\text{C}$.

question: A piece of ice falls from a height $h$ so that it completely melts upon hitting the ground. If only $50\%$ of the energy is retained by the ice, calculate the height $h$. (Take $L_f = 3.36 \times 10^5\text{ J/kg}, g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
explanation: $0.50 (m g h) = m L_f \implies h = \frac{2 L_f}{g} = \frac{2 \times 3.36 \times 10^5}{10} = 6.72 \times 10^4\text{ m} = 67.2\text{ km}$.

subject: Physics
question: Two solid spheres of radii $R$ and $2R$ made of same material are heated to the same initial temperature $T_0$ and allowed to cool in identical environments. The ratio of their initial rates of heat loss $\frac{dQ_1/dt}{dQ_2/dt}$ is:
explanation: Rate of heat loss by radiation $e \sigma A (T^4 - T_0^4) \propto A \propto R^2$. Ratio $\frac{dQ_1/dt}{dQ_2/dt} = \frac{R^2}{(2R)^2} = \frac{1}{4}$.

question: A calorimeter of water equivalent $W = 20\text{ g}$ contains $80\text{ g}$ of water at $15^\circ\text{C}$. Steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$ is passed through it until the temperature rises to $45^\circ\text{C}$. The mass of steam condensed is:
explanation: Heat Gained by (Water + Calorimeter) $= (80 + 20) \times 1 \times (45 - 15) = 100 \times 30 = 3000\text{ cal}$. Heat Lost by Steam of mass $m_s$: $m_s L_v + m_s s_w (100 - 45) = m_s(540 + 55) = 595 m_s$. Equating: $595 m_s = 3000 \implies m_s = \frac{3000}{595} \approx 5.0\text{ g}$.

question: A $20\text{ g}$ piece of copper at $200^\circ\text{C}$ is dropped into a calorimeter containing $100\text{ g}$ of oil at $20^\circ\text{C}$. If the final temperature is $30^\circ\text{C}$ and calorimeter water equivalent is negligible ($s_{\text{Cu}} = 0.1\text{ cal/g }^\circ\text{C}$), the specific heat of the oil is:
explanation: Heat Lost by Cu $= 20 \times 0.1 \times (200 - 30) = 2 \times 170 = 340\text{ cal}$. Heat Gained by oil $= 100 \times s_{\text{oil}} \times (30 - 20) = 1000 s_{\text{oil}}$. Equating: $1000 s_{\text{oil}} = 340 \implies s_{\text{oil}} = 0.34\text{ cal/g }^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: An iron block of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ is dropped from height $h = 84\text{ m}$. Assuming $50\%$ of potential energy is converted to thermal energy of the block, calculate its temperature rise. (Take $s_{\text{iron}} = 420\text{ J/kg K}, g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
explanation: Heat absorbed $Q = 0.50 m g h = 0.50 \times 1 \times 10 \times 84 = 420\text{ J}$. Temperature rise $\Delta T = \frac{Q}{m s} = \frac{420}{1 \times 420} = 1.0^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: $40\text{ g}$ of ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is added to $200\text{ g}$ of water at $40^\circ\text{C}$. The final equilibrium temperature of the mixture is:
explanation: Heat required to melt $40\text{ g}$ ice: $40 \times 80 = 3200\text{ cal}$. Heat lost by $200\text{ g}$ water to reach temp $T$: $200 \times 1 \times (40 - T) = 3200 + 40 \times 1 \times T \implies 8000 - 200 T = 3200 + 40 T \implies 240 T = 4800 \implies T = 20^\circ\text{C}$.
